question: Is focused runner/Codex regression proof enough to merge this Codex lane-release fix after the dirty head is refreshed, or should maintainers require live wedge proof first?
rationale: The code path and regression support the fix, but merging changes when same-session work is released while Codex cleanup may still be unresolved, and the PR has an explicit human-review/proof-decision signal.

options.title: Accept Focused Proof After Refresh
options.body: Resolve the dirty merge state, rerun checks on the exact refreshed head, and merge using the focused runner regression as sufficient proof for the lane-release contract.

options.title: Require Live Wedge Proof
options.body: Pause merge until a live or Crabbox Codex app-server wedge, ideally with channel delivery evidence, proves the cleanup overlap is acceptable.

options.title: Pause The Replacement
options.body: Keep or close the replacement if maintainers no longer want to pursue this candidate fix for the linked production stall.

recommendation.title: Accept Focused Proof After Refresh
recommendation.body: Resolve the dirty merge state, rerun checks on the exact refreshed head, and merge using the focused runner regression as sufficient proof for the lane-release contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged and contributed to the adjacent native lane-release contract that this PR extends, making him the strongest available owner for the proof and merge-risk call.
